title: Thiol-ene microfluidic chip for fast on-chip sample clean-up, separation and ESI mass analysis of peptides and proteins
projectDescription: Microfluidic devices coupled to MS promises low manufacturing costs, low sample consumption and channels with a high surface area to volume ratio and tailorable functional groups. Here, we describe a thiol-ene-based microfluidic chip that is capable of sample loading, desalting and on-chip reversed phase chromatography prior to on-chip electrospray ionization for the intact analysis of proteins and peptides, as well as, for on-chip bottom-up proteomics workflows coupled directly with mass spectrometry.
sampleProcessingProtocol: The samples are mostly non-treated protein and peptide spiked samples, except for a single offline experiment with tryptic digestion of hemoglobin later used to test trapping of peptides on the on-chip packed bed.
dataProcessingProtocol: The data was analyzed solely in full scan mode (MS only), proteins was deconvoluted using Waters MassLynx software (MaxEnt) and Magtran (by Zhongqi Zhang and Alan G. Marshall). Peptide mapping was performed according to in-silico tryptic digests using the software GPMAW (General Protein/Mass Analysis for Windows, Lighthouse data, Odense Denmark) as presented in Peri, S.; Steen, H.; Pandey, A. GPMAW – a Software Tool for Analyzing Proteins and Peptides. Trends Biochem. Sci. 2001, 26 (11), 687–689. https://doi.org/10.1016/S0968-0004(01)01954-5.
